slo_documented.detail: SLOs supplied externally by the orchestrator (p95 < 200ms excl. model, max 20% regression). Not embedded in a test file, slo.yaml, or code annotation within the repo. Acceptable for a hackathon story with a justified perf_tests_required=false ruling, but a slo.yaml or inline @slo annotation would make this self-documenting.
slo_documented.recommendation: Add a slo.yaml or @slo JSDoc annotation to lib/match/run-staffing-search.ts before SKILL-6 productionisation.

findings.detail: buildMatchDataset issues a single prisma.employee.findMany with a nested select { skills: { select: { trustState, skill: { name } } } }. Prisma batches the relation load — no per-profile query loop. No N+1.
Route is strictly read-only (no DB writes anywhere in the SKILL-3 surface). No read-then-write pattern exists. No atomicity violation.
Only one external call per path: one prisma.employee.findMany in buildMatchDataset, one callClaude in runStaffingSearch. Never more than one sequential call to the same dependency in a single method.
No cache TTL or expiry is set in any SKILL-3 file. Prompt-cache lifetime is managed entirely by Anthropic's infrastructure. No jitter concern.
No write operations exist; there is no read-after-write pattern anywhere in the route.

prisma.employee.findMany for MANAGER/ADMIN scope has no `take` limit. At ~25 synthetic profiles (demo scale) this is benign and within the p95 SLO. At org scale (thousands of employees) this would: (a) blow the Anthropic context window for the serialized dataset, and (b) increase serialization and prompt-cache assembly time beyond the 200ms SLO. Acceptable for SKILL-3 hackathon scope but must be addressed before production.
findings.recommendation: Add a configurable `take` cap (e.g. 200 profiles) with a deterministic sort before the findMany, and document the window-size constraint in a TODO comment.

findings.detail: The PRACTICE_LEAD scope filters on `where: { leadId: session.employeeId }` (dataset.ts:67). The Employee.leadId field has no @@index in the schema. For SQLite with 25 rows this is a full-table scan but sub-millisecond. At scale (hundreds of employees per practice), lack of index on leadId degrades the scoped dataset fetch. Acceptable at current demo scale.
findings.recommendation: Add @@index([leadId]) to the Employee model before scaling beyond demo data.

prompt_cache_validation.detail: RANKING_RULES_PROMPT + serialized dataset are concatenated as `cacheableContext` and passed as the `system` argument to callClaude (run-staffing-search.ts:90-98). The per-request query is rendered only into the user turn via matchStaffingPrompt (match-staffing.ts). This is the correct cache breakpoint: the large, stable system block is cacheable across queries; the small volatile user turn is not. Confirmed by test S3-P1-02 and S3-P3-06.

p95_excl_model.detail: Non-Claude route work per request: (1) JSON.parse of request body — O(1); (2) buildMatchDataset — one prisma.employee.findMany + in-process row mapping, O(n) with n~25; (3) serializeDataset — in-memory Array.sort + JSON.stringify, O(n log n) with n~25; (4) result mapping + Response.json — O(k) where k = shortlist size. All operations are in-process or single-round-trip DB. At n=25 the total non-model path is estimated well under 20ms, leaving an 180ms margin against the 200ms SLO. No measurable runtime evidence available (NO_LIVE_CLIENT stub).
p95_excl_model.measurability: NOT_MEASURABLE — NO_LIVE_CLIENT active; actual latency deferred to Tier-2 smoke / Tier-3 perf environment

regression.detail: No prior run to compare against. Regression gate is vacuously satisfied for the first delivery but must be established in Tier-3 as the baseline for SKILL-4 and later.
